messages:
Samir: Support ticket from EU customers — p99 latency spike on /v1/generate since ~09:07 UTC, TLS handshake times jumping +200-400ms. Graphs: https://grafana.company/reports/abc123
Mia: Which region? eu-west-1 or eu-west-2?
Samir: eu-west-1 only. Affects hosted API and some dedicated nodes behind the same POP.
Oliver: Ran a quick traceroute from probe in FR -> got an unexpected cross-AZ hop into eu-west-2 before coming back. snippet:
  1 10.1.0.1
  2 100.64.10.3 (eu-west-2-edge)
  3 10.2.0.5 (eu-west-1)
Looks like GSLB/anycast choosing a weird path.
Jess (oncall): Can you paste a curl -w report and a tcpdump SYN/ACK timeline for one of the requests? Need to see retransmits.
Samir: curl output:
  time_connect: 0.050
  time_appconnect: 0.602
  time_starttransfer: 0.632
tcpdump shows SYN, SYN-ACK, then client retransmit 2x, then final ACK ~350ms later. SYN retransmits = handshake retry behaviour.
Mia: DNS eval: dig +short api.redwood.dev from FR probe returns rotating set of anycast IPs, TTL=20s. One of the IPs maps to eu-west-2 ASN via bgpmon: https://bgp.company/changes/8472
ops-bot: bgp-update detected for prefix 203.0.113.0/24 shifted to peer AS64512 at 09:05 UTC.
Oliver: That BGP flapping explains path bounce -> extra latency for TLS initial packets (handshake state across different POPs). Could cause KV cache misses too.
Jess (oncall): Immediate mitigation options:
  - pin customers to eu-west-1 anycast IP (disable GSLB rotation for affected prefixes)
  - increase TLS keepalive time on edge so handshakes less frequent
  - temporary route prepend to prefer eu-west-1
Which is fastest?
Mia: Pinning prefix via our traffic-control quickpatch is fastest. I'll push a canary to 5% then 100% if green.
Samir: Can you also add a filter to route-probe to drop eu-west-2 choices so new DNS answers avoid that POP?
Mia: Patching now: `trafficctl set-affinity --prefix 203.0.113.0/24 --prefer-pop eu-west-1 --canary 0.05`
ops-bot: trafficctl: canary update started (id=canary-992)
Oliver: Monitoring p95/p99 on the canary — initial 5% shows handshake lat normalized from ~600ms -> ~120ms.
Mia: Rolling to 100% now.
ops-bot: trafficctl: canary complete -> applied to 100%
Samir: After full roll: p99 dropped back to baseline within 3m. Support emailed customers with ETA + root cause in progress.
Jess (oncall): Follow-ups: get BGP teammate to investigate why prefix was announced from eu-west-2, increase DNS TTL to 60s for steady-state, and add probe to detect cross-pop handoffs earlier. I'll file infra ticket.
Samir: Filed INFRA-2124 with logs and tcpdump links.
Oliver: Leaving this thread open until BGP root cause is determined. For now mitigation in place.
ops-bot: incident: resolved — latency spike mitigated (runbook applied).
